findings.question: q-chemistry-periodic-table-0009
findings.quote: Nitrogen has a higher first ionization energy than carbon. In this comparison, the increased effective nuclear attraction across period 2 supports the observed ordering.
findings.problem: The central reason is left in technical language rather than Grade 5 plain English. A learner who does not understand “effective nuclear attraction” is told the ranking but cannot follow why nitrogen needs more energy to lose an electron.
findings.fix: Say that nitrogen has more protons pulling on electrons in the same outer layer, so it holds its outer electrons more tightly and takes more energy to remove one.
